body: ADR-218 was built, verified -- 53 mutants all killed, the ledger says so -- and never delivered: its paragraph, its board row, its runner's ledger entry and its run_all line reached origin inside ADR-217's commit, and tools/exempt.py, tools/audit_declared.py, verify_declared and mutate_declared existed nowhere (ADR-219). This is that slice again, built from its paragraph and the names of its mutants, which together turned out to be a specification. THE DEFECT: six audits let a finding be DECLARED with a reason and all six applied the exemption by filtering the finding out of the list and writing the FILTERED list to the ledger, so the evidence was discarded at the moment the exemption was used; a declaration is keyed by a label, a label is not a durable identity, and an exemption that outlives its subject does not fail loudly, it sits there being green. Six audits could add one and none could remove one. Thirty stood. NOW tools/exempt.py is the only place an exemption is granted and it FILTERS AND RECORDS IN ONE CALL: the row gets raw (what was flagged before the exemption) and seen (everything the reading could have flagged) beside the filtered list, as copies; a blank reason is refused there, once; an audit with two ratchets on one row keeps two records and the whole-page declaration gets the audit's own verdict written to the row. All six audits go through it. tools/audit_declared.py reads what that writes and gives every declaration one of four verdicts -- COVERING, IDLE (slack that would hide the defect coming back), STALE (nothing by that name), UNREAD (no row, no universe, or a row older than the newest row of its own one-pass ledger by more than six hours) -- and only covering passes; a page that has grown an export is STALE for its no-outputs declaration because it is not the page the reason was about; the contention ledger is a sweep, not a pass, and gets no freshness test, stated per source. It has no --declare, deliberately: it can only take a declaration away, and --forget prints the reason it removes. verify_declared 48 builds ledgers where each verdict is the right one, drives --forget through every refusal, and then holds the LIVE ledgers to the rule: filtered within raw within seen, and raw minus filtered exactly the declared keys. mutate_declared 45 all killed; the shared rule is asserted through each of the six audits' own suites and mutated through their six runners with exempt.py in each subject. WHAT THE REBUILD FOUND ABOUT ITSELF: a fixture whose newest row was NOW could not tell a reader that measured age against the clock from one that measured it against the ledger, and the mutant survived until the newest row was moved a thousand seconds back; eight mutants crashed the suite instead of failing it, and the suite reads every row with .get now. THE FIRST HONEST READING against the live ledgers is in the ADR.
subject: ADR-224: thirty written judgements stood in four ledgers and nothing could say whether one of them was still about anything (ADR-218, rebuilt)
